_comment: Domain knowledge that no general-purpose embedding model carries: which documents evidence which
requirement. An advisor asking for 'address proof' wants the electricity bill, but the bill talks about
meter readings and direct debits — all five embedding models measured on this corpus ranked it 13th or
worse for that query while ranking every other probe first.
A query reaches a rule by meaning, not by containing one of its phrases: the concept and its paraphrases
are embedded at startup, and the rule fires when the query comes within search.concept-floor of one of
them and search.concept-floor-ratio of the best rule's score. So paraphrases are examples, not a list to
complete — state the requirement as an advisor would, and keep out acronyms and words every query about a
person carries ('client', 'he', 'her'), which drag unrelated queries in.
A rule carries two lists, split by which arm can use them. document_types is what an advisor CALLS the
document ('utility bill'): embedded at startup and run as semantic probes, four per query. document_phrases
is text the DOCUMENT ITSELF carries in its own words ('supply address', 'gross pay', 'proprietorship
register'): never embedded, run as one extra full-text query and as sparse probes, because such a phrase IS
the exact token those arms exist to match — where a type name is not, since a document never says what type
it is. Order matters in both: the first four types are the semantic budget and the first four phrases are
the sparse one, while the full-text side takes them all in one scan.
Types come from the governing text and adviser practice, ordered by how commonly a client file holds one.
Phrases must be text a real document of one of that rule's types carries: EvidenceFixtureTest gates each
one — at least two lexemes after stemming, no match against any rule's concept, paraphrases or types (a
phrase that restates a type name reproduces the bug this split fixes), a carrier among that rule's own
documents, and reachable through the arm. The seeded demo corpus decides neither list — it is twenty
documents and lacks most of these types, so 'reaches nothing seeded' is a fact about the seed.
After editing run ConceptFloorTest (the floors, the sibling matrix and the listed exceptions) and
EvidenceFixtureTest, which holds one held-out document per type and asserts that each probe places its
own. Every rule's source, what each probe reaches, the requirements enumerated and rejected, and why this
mapping is configuration rather than something a model could learn: docs/search-design.md, 'Where the
lexicon comes from'.
